item.title: A Deep-Dive Keynote at the 34th IPMA World Congress: Leadership Under Extreme Conditions
item.description: Only 40 percent of project leaders in large-scale projects feel confident they will successfully reach their goals. In other words, the majority do not believe in the success of their own initiatives. In stark contrast, cave diving—projects in themselves with clear start and end points and inherent risks—must succeed 100 percent of the time.

item.title: Agile Leadership in an Apple Streaming Series: Can Ted Lasso Inspire Project Management Professionals?
item.description: You may be wondering what goldfish have to do with agile leadership. The answer will be shared by Constantin Hoya in his talk “Agile Leadership: Lessons from Ted Lasso” at the upcoming 34th IPMA World Congress. Breaking away from the tradition of explaining leadership concepts purely in academic terms, he uses the popular Apple TV series Ted Lasso to illustrate ideas for Agile Leadership.

item.title: Project Leadership: Embracing the Conundrum
item.description: At the IPMA World Congress Berlin 2025, David Hudson presented “Project Leadership – The Conundrum,” a session that resonated with many of us who live the challenges of leading projects every day. Hudson reminded us that leadership is not a formula or a fixed trait. Instead, it is a paradox: a balancing act between aspiration and perfection, between leading and influencing, and between what we know, what we can do, and who we are under pressure. item.title: Panel Discussion at the 34th IPMA World Congress: Presidential Quartet Looks Ahead to the Future of Project Management
item.description: At this year’s IPMA World Congress, current President Mladen Vukomanović joined three of his predecessors – Brigitte Schaden, Roberto Mori and Joop Schefferlie – for a panel discussion on the history, core values and future challenges of the International Project Management Association (IPMA). The “Insights Session” provided an intimate setting to reflect on how the role of the project manager must evolve in a world shaped by disruptive technologies and increasing social responsibility.

item.title: Marking 100 Years of Roland W. Gutsch: From Network Planning to Global Cooperation
item.description: This month marks what would have been the 100th birthday of Professor Dr Roland W. Gutsch, the founder of the German Project Management Association (GPM) and one of the pioneers of modern project management. A visionary engineer and networker long before the term became fashionable, Gutsch recognised that successful projects depend not only on technical precision but also on structure, collaboration, and international exchange.

item.description: IPMA Global Project Profession Forum 2026 brought together an extraordinary panel of current and past leaders of the project profession to reflect on decisions, values, and the future direction of project management in an era defined by AI, sustainability, and societal transformation.
